title: Phase-hedging prefill/decode scheduler: latency-first hedges with throughput-safe fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: At high utilization, existing prefill+decode scheduler either optimizes for bulk throughput (sacrificing tail latency for small interactive requests) or for strict per-request fairness which decreases overall GPU utilization. We need a hybrid policy that: (1) reduces 95/99th decode latency for small/interactive requests, (2) preserves sustained throughput for bulk workloads, and (3) avoids starvation and KV-cache thrashing.
goal: Design and implement a 'phase-hedging' scheduler that splits requests into micro-phases, opportunistically hedges GPU resources for latency-sensitive tails, and falls back to throughput-optimized consolidation when utilization is constrained.
acceptance_criteria: E2E integration tests for scheduling invariants (no deadlocks, no request loss)
Real workload benchmark: 95th decode latency for <128-token queries reduced by >=25% at 60% GPU util compared to baseline scheduler
Overall tokens/sec drop <= 7% for typical throughput jobs when hedging is enabled
Starvation metric (requests waiting > SLO) under mixed traffic <= prior baseline
KV cache locality regression <= 2% for pinned sessions
Feature gated and rolloutable with canary AB test and automatic circuit-breaker on QPS/latency regressions

design_decisions: Use micro-phase window of 8 tokens as default; reasoning: balances KV cache locality and enables low-latency hedges for short responses
Hedging model: spawn low-cost speculative decode slots on idle SMs for latency-sensitive buckets; speculative slots expire after 'hedge_timeout' (default 15ms)
Avoid hard preemption of in-flight long prefills; instead prefer opportunistic hedges until system reaches 'hedge_backoff_util' threshold (default 85% GPU util)
Fairness accounting: introduce 'hedge_credits' that decay over time to ensure bulk traffic gets compensated; credits derive from tokens generated by the session
Integrate with kernel selector: hedged slots prefer small-sequence fused attention kernels when available to reduce per-token SM overhead
Fallback: when hedging causes throughput regression beyond configured tolerance, automatically switch to throughput-first consolidation policy
experiments: A/B canary v1: 10% of pools with hedging enabled vs baseline (ran 2026-02-22 to 2026-03-01)
Microbenchmark: 95th latency for short queries dropped 32% with fused attention + hedging enabled on A100 (results in /dash/hedge-v1)
Throughput test: small tokens/sec regression of 5% at 70% util; acceptable per acceptance criteria
KV-cache study: no more than 1.7% increase in cold misses when micro-phase=8; larger micro-phases increased misses substantially

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV-cache fragmentation leading to throughput regressions. Mitigation: cap micro-phase length; tie hedging to session affinity when available.

Risk: Hedging increases SM context switches on some GPUs and hurts absolute throughput. Mitigation: kernel-selector policy: only spawn hedged slots when fused-small kernels available or when SM idle windows detected.
Risk: Unexpected fairness regressions for enterprise reserved capacity customers. Mitigation: feature off by default for Dedicated pools and require opt-in via console until stable.
Risk: Complexity in rollout and observability. Mitigation: circuit-breaker metrics, automatic rollback on latency or tokens/sec regressions, clear runbook
notes: Next steps: finalize default heuristics after 2 weeks of canary traffic; add opt-out flag per-customer for Dedicated; coordinate with kernel team to expose small-seq fused kernel availability in runtime kernel selector API
Consider follow-up: adaptive micro-phase sizing based on per-session sequence length distribution and token entropy
